chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi al-Bilad who said:

Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: 'What has become of the wretched Hamza ibn Bazi?' I said: 'He has arrived.' He said: 'He claims that my father is alive! They are today among the doubters, and they will not die tomorrow except upon heresy (al-zandaqa).' Safwan said: 'I said to myself: I know them as doubters, so how can they die upon heresy?' We did not wait long until it reached us that one of them said at the time of his death: 'I am a disbeliever in my Lord who caused me to die!' Safwan said: 'This is confirmation of the tradition.'

key_terms.الشَّقِيُّ: The wretched/fortunate one (used for Hamza ibn Bazi)
key_terms.الشُّكَّاكٌ: The doubters (those who doubted the Imam's death)
key_terms.حَمْزَةُ بْنُ بَزِيعٍ: Hamza ibn Bazi, a key figure among the Waqifites

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida predict about the death of Hamza ibn Bazi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological dispute with the Waqifites, who halted their belief in the Imamate at Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.), claiming he did not die. Imam al-Rida (a.s.) distinguishes between mere doubt (*shaka*) and the specific heresy (*zindqa*) of denying death, predicting that Hamza ibn Bazi’s followers would ultimately declare disbelief in the Lord who caused the death they denied. This narrative serves as a critical validation of the eventual death of the Imams, countering the Waqifite claim of their perpetual presence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 72 - Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Yahya has narrated from his father from Muhammad bin Hasan bin Abil Khattab from Safwan bin Yahya that he said: Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Balad said:

Imam Ridha (a.s) said: What did Hamza bin Bazi, the unfortunate one do? I replied: He has also come. Imam (a.s) said: He thinks that my father is alive, they [Hamza and his associates] are in doubt today and tomorrow they would not die, except as heretics. Safwan says: I said to myself: I knew that they are among doubters, but how can they die disbelievers and heretics? Not much time passed when I received information that one of them said at the time of his death: I am a disbeliever in my Lord who wants me to die. Safwan says: I said: This testifies for that same tradition [of the Imam].
